title: Pre-compile schema and consumer validation in persona compiler

sections.what: Execute strict pre-compile validation before running `compile_persona()`. Refuse compile or highlight issues if required schema fields are missing, invalid data types are present, or known consumers cannot parse the structured values.
sections.why: Compiling an incomplete or broken persona block currently generates broken or empty prose segments (e.g. `None` strings, incomplete sentences, or malformed tag lists) that overwrite working authored prose.
sections.how:
- In `engine/character_appearance.py`, introduce `validate_before_compile(record: dict) -> tuple[bool, list[str]]`.
- Check required types, age ranges, gender/pronoun consistency, and slug conformity.
- Return structured error summaries in `POST /api/players/<name>/record/compile`.
- Prevent accidental overwrite if critical validation errors exist.

acceptance.text: `compile_persona` refuses compile if critical validation errors exist, returning actionable reasons.
Warning-level issues are reported without blocking compilation when safe.
Unit tests cover validation rejections and safe compilations.
